keyQuotes: JetBrains evaluated coding agents on the things that matter in practice: can they solve real software engineering tasks, quickly and at a cost that makes sense.

mainPoints.explanation: The evaluation used 225 Java, 38 C#, and 90 Python tasks from real codebases, measuring solve rate, cost, and latency. Codex with GPT-5.4-mini medium reasoning achieved the best overall balance.
mainPoints.point: Codex was selected as the recommended agent based on a systematic evaluation across three ecosystem benchmarks.

mainPoints.explanation: This ensures the recommendation is practical for typical users, not just the most powerful model.
mainPoints.point: Cost constraints were applied early: setups that would push more than 2% of users over $20/month were ruled out before ranking on quality and latency.

mainPoints.explanation: Codex outperformed Junie in the A/B test, which tipped the decision despite close offline results.
mainPoints.point: The offline benchmark was validated with an online A/B test tracking real user behavior (engagement, agent switching, failure rate).

mainPoints.explanation: This highlights a commitment to data-driven iteration rather than a fixed choice.
mainPoints.point: The recommendation is not permanent; JetBrains will re-evaluate as models evolve, agents join, and benchmark coverage grows.

oneSentenceSummary: JetBrains announces Codex as the recommended default agent in JetBrains AI, based on systematic evaluation across real-world coding benchmarks and online A/B testing.
originalTitle: Introducing the Recommended Agent in AI Chat with Codex as the current choice
summary: This post explains how JetBrains selected Codex (powered by OpenAI) as the recommended coding agent in JetBrains AI. The evaluation used a benchmark dataset of real software engineering tasks across Java, C#, and Python, measuring solve rate, cost, and latency. After comparing candidates (including Junie with Gemini models), Codex with GPT-5.4-mini medium reasoning emerged as the top performer in both offline benchmarks and online A/B tests. The article details the methodology, including cost constraints (avoiding more than 2% of users exceeding $20/month), and provides transparent data via the DPAIA repository. It also emphasizes that users can still switch agents freely.
title: Introducing the Recommended Agent in AI Chat with Codex as the current choice
